questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: South Korea was the obvious choice for me since I study Korean studies and had a mandatory semester abroad. But even if I wasn't a Korean studies major, I would still have chosen South Korea, because the culture and university structure is different from Denmark, and I thought it would be really interesting to explore something completely different than Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Covid-19 sadly affected my semester abroad a lot.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was both easy and hard - I had to be really careful and make sure I had everything under control related to covid-19 restrictions and such. But all other information - how to apply directly to the University, how to apply for a visa, how to find recommendation was simple.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yonsei University's study abroad department was really helpful throughout everything and so was the study abroad department at KU.  I received assistance from KU with forhåndsgodkendelse and what to do if I couldn't get the courses that I needed. From Yonsei I received assistance with course registration, how and where to pick up my student ID, how to apply for Korean registration card, sim card registration and how to navigate the covid-19 restrictions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. Many different options such as airbnb, student housing off campus etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's best to find something close to campus so it's easy and fast to go to class.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you want to live in a dorm at Yonsei, you have to be aware that there are not a lot of spots available. Sadly, an American study abroad program booked the majority of the rooms for their own students, so not a lot of room were available for everyone else. It's best to have a plan B.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bidding system. We had 72 points each we could use on the courses we needed. Those who bid the highest, is registered to the course. It's a good idea to check out how many point were needed to get into the course the previous years - that what I did. For KLI (the language program) they have unlimited spots, so you can bid 1 point and get in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the administration and they would try to help the best they could. The professors were also helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the amount of points were needed the previous years and try to aim above that when bidding points. if you don't get your class, try and contact the professor. Most of them are really helpful and will register you for the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The language program was really really good. i learned a lot. But the other classes were kinda easy compared to the classes in Denmark, so I wasn't challenged academically.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For the regular classes, there wasn't any student involvement. We just listened to the professor throughout the entire class and that was it. For the language program, it was very much like how it is at Copenhagen which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intensive Korean Language program level 3 (KLI)
Contemporary Korean Cinema and Society
Korea-US relations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend KLI as it was really challenging and I learned a lot. We were forced to speak a lot which helped.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't remember any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than I thought. it's definitely possible to find something cheaper. Also, the books-section was a one time payment, so I paid 500kr once for my books.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a buddy-program, but we weren't informed about until after the deadline which was a shame because I really wanted to join that program

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing because of the covid-19 situation

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you can, join the buddy program.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All of the historical sights are really beautiful. I also really liked Lotte World and enjoyed my time there. Explore the restaurants behind the busy streets and in the basements. The more it's hidden the better the food is.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Both easy and hard. I knew what to expect but it was also difficult to navigate.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be nice and you'll be fine.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The not talking on public transportation rule. I still find it odd.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How nice most people were and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to hang out with other exchange students, explore outside of the city and try to hang out with the locals.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The language program and talking to locals

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living alone in a foreign country where most people don't speak English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
